Definition: Frequency and severity of power outages experienced by businesses and households. Based on World Bank Enterprise Surveys, Afrobarometer, or national utility data. Reflects the quality of electricity supply beyond mere access — critical for running ICT equipment and data infrastructure.
Value Name: Severe (frequent daily outages or regular load shedding)
Comments: South Africa experienced widespread load-shedding with many days affected (e.g., 335 days with load-shedding in 2023), indicating severe reliability issues (daily/regular outages).
revision_notes: Original score (1=Severe) rested on a 2023 FTI Consulting commentary citing 335 days of loadshedding that year; this figure is corroborated and superseded by the CSIR's 2024 Utility-Scale Power Generation Statistics report, which confirms 2023 was a record loadshedding year. Eskom's own operational updates and the CSIR report show a dramatic turnaround from April 2024 onward: Energy Availability Factor rose from ~55% (2023) to ~60% (2024) to 70%+ by late 2025, loadshedding fell by ~76% in 2024 versus 2023 (281 consecutive loadshedding-free days by 31 Dec 2024), and only a handful of loadshedding occasions occurred in FY2024/25 with none recorded from mid-May to at least late December 2025. Taken alone, this generation-level data would support a much higher score (Good/4 or higher). However, Wetility's 2025 national telemetry dataset (91,934 unique outage events sampled across 9 provinces and 57 municipalities) shows households still experienced an average of 6-9 discrete power outages per month through 2025, mostly attributable to municipal distribution-network faults rather than national generation shortfalls. Since the variable specifically asks about outages 'experienced by businesses and households' rather than Eskom loadshedding stages alone, I have set the revised code to 2 (Poor: weekly outages) as the best-supported reading of actual experienced reliability, but this is flagged for human review given the substantial gap between the generation-level and distribution-level evidence and the scale of change from the original score.
revised_comments: Eskom's national loadshedding programme has largely stopped since mid-2024, with the utility reporting an Energy Availability Factor above 70% and more than 200 consecutive days without scheduled outages by late 2025. Despite this generation-level recovery, independent household telemetry covering nine provinces records ongoing frequent local power interruptions, averaging six to nine outage events per household per month through 2025, mostly linked to municipal distribution-network faults rather than national supply shortfalls. Overall reliability has therefore improved substantially from the severe 2023 loadshedding crisis, but households and businesses continue to experience regular, often lengthy, outages at the distribution level.

Definition: Percentage of total electricity generation from renewable sources (hydro, solar, wind, geothermal, biomass). Indicates energy sustainability and potential for distributed power solutions relevant to ICT infrastructure in off-grid areas.
Comments: IEA Bioenergy country report notes electricity had a renewable share of 8.8% in 2023 (7.9% in 2022), which is <10%.
revision_notes: Original score (1=<10%) was based on an IEA Bioenergy country report figure of 8.8% for 2023. Checked against the CSIR's 2024 Utility-Scale Power Generation Statistics report (published 2025), which gives combined CSP/solar/wind/other generation of 17.8 TWh plus hydro of 1.1 TWh against total generation of 221.2 TWh in 2024 — a combined renewable share of approximately 8.5%, marginally lower than 2023 due to reduced hydro inflows despite continued solar/wind capacity additions. The IEA's South Africa country page corroborates a single-digit-percentage renewables share of total generation. The score is confirmed unchanged at 1 (<10%), with the underlying year updated to reflect 2024 data.
revised_comments: Renewable sources (solar, wind, concentrated solar power and hydro) supplied approximately 8.5% of South Africa's utility-scale electricity generation in 2024 (around 18.9 TWh of a 221.2 TWh total), according to the CSIR's Utility-Scale Power Generation Statistics report. Coal remains dominant, accounting for over 80% of generation, with the renewable share broadly flat compared with 2023 as reduced hydro output largely offset continued growth in solar and wind capacity. This keeps the renewable generation share below the 10% threshold.
